events.text: US BLS Employment Situation released Jan 10 2025: December 2024 nonfarm payroll employment rose by 256,000; unemployment rate was 4.1%.
events.market_expectation: Econoday survey pre-release consensus: nonfarm payrolls +157000; unemployment 4.2%.

events.text: US BLS CPI released Jan 15 2025: December 2024 seasonally adjusted CPI rose 0.4% month over month, while unadjusted annual CPI rose 2.9%.
events.market_expectation: Reuters economist pre-release poll as reported Jan 15: headline CPI +0.3% m/m; +2.9% y/y.

events.text: Bank of Japan Jan 24 2025 monetary policy statement: raised its uncollateralized overnight call rate target to around 0.5%, effective Jan 27. BOJ stated that real interest rates were expected to remain significantly negative and further tightening would depend on the outlook.
events.observed_result: Rate target increased to around 0.5%, effective Jan 27

events.text: US Federal Reserve FOMC Jan 29 2025 statement: maintained the federal funds target range at 4.25% to 4.50%. The statement described continued solid economic expansion and somewhat elevated inflation.
US BLS Employment Situation released Feb 7 2025: January 2025 nonfarm payrolls increased 143,000; unemployment rate declined to 4.0%.
events.market_expectation: Econoday survey pre-release consensus: nonfarm payrolls +168000; unemployment 4.1%.

events.text: US BLS CPI released Feb 12 2025: January 2025 seasonally adjusted CPI rose 0.5% month over month; unadjusted 12-month increase was 3.0%.
events.market_expectation: Econoday survey pre-release consensus: headline CPI +0.3% m/m; +2.9% y/y.

events.text: US BLS Employment Situation released Mar 7 2025: February 2025 nonfarm payroll employment increased by 151,000; unemployment rate was 4.1%.
events.market_expectation: Econoday survey pre-release consensus: nonfarm payrolls +160000; unemployment 4.0%.

events.text: US BLS CPI released Mar 12 2025: February 2025 seasonally adjusted headline CPI rose 0.2% m/m and 2.8% y/y unadjusted.
events.market_expectation: CME/Econoday Market Focus Mar 12 (before release): headline CPI +0.3% m/m; +2.9% y/y.

events.text: Bank of Japan Mar 19 2025 monetary policy statement: retained the overnight call rate target at around 0.5%. It characterized the economy as recovering moderately and recent ex-fresh-food CPI inflation as around 3.0-3.5%.

US Federal Reserve FOMC Mar 19 2025 statement: maintained policy rate target at 4.25%-4.50%; announced slower decline of Treasury holdings from April, reducing monthly Treasury redemption cap from $25 billion to $5 billion.
events.observed_result: Held 4.25%-4.50%; Treasury runoff cap to $5bn in April

events.text: US BLS March 2025 CPI release: headline fell 0.1% month over month on a seasonally adjusted basis; rose 2.4% over 12 months.
US BEA advance GDP estimate for 2025 Q1 released April 30: real GDP decreased at a 0.3% annual rate; rise in imports and decline in government spending weighed on headline growth.
events.observed_result: Real GDP -0.3% annual rate, 2025 Q1 advance estimate

events.text: US FOMC May 7 2025 statement kept federal funds rate target 4.25%-4.50%; noted elevated uncertainty and risks to both employment and inflation.
US BLS April 2025 CPI release: headline increased 0.2% seasonally adjusted month over month and 2.3% over 12 months.
US BLS May 2025 CPI release: headline increased 0.1% seasonally adjusted month over month and 2.4% over 12 months.
US FOMC June 18 2025 statement maintained target range at 4.25%-4.50%. Unemployment remained low; inflation remained somewhat elevated.
US BLS June 2025 CPI release: headline increased 0.3% seasonally adjusted month over month and 2.7% over 12 months.
US FOMC July 30 2025 statement maintained federal funds rate target 4.25%-4.50%; two members voted for a 25bp reduction.
US BLS July 2025 CPI release: headline increased 0.2% seasonally adjusted month over month and 2.7% over 12 months.
US BLS August 2025 CPI release: headline increased 0.4% seasonally adjusted month over month and 2.9% over 12 months.
US FOMC September 17 2025 statement reduced the federal funds target range by 0.25 percentage points to 4.00%-4.25% and cited rising downside employment risk.
US FOMC October 29 2025 statement reduced the federal funds target range by 0.25 percentage points to 3.75%-4.00%; said balance-sheet runoff would stop December 1.
US FOMC December 10 2025 statement reduced the federal funds target range by 0.25 percentage points to 3.50%-3.75%; noted labor market softening and elevated inflation.
